b: The Weeknd has spent his stadium tour writing songs for the cities he plays, and his ode to Hong Kong has traveled a lot farther than Kai Tak Stadium. Today he released a music video for “Hong Kong,” his collaboration with Cantopop icon Faye Wong. Directed by Evan Larsen, the clip stars Chinese supermodel Ming Xi and was shot across Mong Kok and Hong Kong Island.

Since its release last month, “Hong Kong,” which is built around Wong’s 1993 ballad “Monsoon,” has been rewriting the record books on Chinese streaming platforms. According to the Weeknd’s camp, it posted the biggest first-day debut for a non-Mandarin song on NetEase Cloud Music in five years, making him the first international artist in that span to top all three of the service’s major charts on release day. On QQ Music, it logged the biggest debut ever for a Western male artist.

The video for “Hong Kong” lands as the Weeknd wraps the Asian leg of his After Hours Til Dawn Stadium Tour. The tour has sold grossed over $1.3 billion across 176 shows, making it the highest-grossing tour ever by a male artist.
